item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00367","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C21","C14","C12"],"selected_candidate_label":"C21","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C21 is a highly plausible material drafting template. It is the same type of letter, issued by the same President to the Attorney General, concerning an unresolved labor dispute at Atomic Energy Commission facilities. The child follows C21's distinctive sequence: creation of a section 206 Board of Inquiry; receipt and attachment of its report; a separate account of the dispute's continued or renewed strike posture at gaseous-diffusion facilities; the finding that the strike affects an entire industry or substantial part thereof and imperils national safety; and a section 208 direction to seek an injunction, secure resumed interstate and foreign commerce, and obtain other relief needed to protect the national interest. C14 and C12 share much of the injunction-letter formula, but lack C21's atomic-energy setting, gaseous-diffusion-plant facts, national-safety-only formulation, and distinctive 'remove a peril' and
